Smart Weighted Hula Hoops for Adults Weight Loss Non-Fall Exercise Hoola Hoop Detachable Adjustable Size Abdomen Fitness Massage Professional Intelligent Counter Workout for Women Men and Kids Blue I looked at tons of weighted hoola hoops on Amazon and saw many of them has some not so great reviews because they were no sturdy or would break apart. This hoola hoop is definitely very sturdy and well made.

It comes in several pieces that link together so you can adjust it to fit your waist and ideally remove pieces as you lose weight. The pieces link together very well, it feels very secure. The weight is also very secure in the hoola hoop.

I find it to be a really fun way to work out. You do feel the burn with this especially if you do the full recommended 30 mins. It took me 2 days to get the hang of it, I watched a couple youtube videos for some tips. Basically, you want to shift your weight side to side rather than do a full circular motion with your hips.

I have been using it for about 2 weeks now - about every other day and I noticed a slight decrease in my waist but nothing crazy yet, though I do believe doing this for a month at least 5 days a week will give you noticeable results.

Currently, I am able to go for about 10 mins straight without stopping at all. Whenever I stop, I switch directions. The only downside that I have noticed is when I use it in the opposite direction, the counter on the hoop doesn't count those spins. It only counts going in one direction. I don't know if that's just something wrong with my counter or if that's how it's made but ultimately it's not that big of an issue (though it would be nice to have an accurate count of my total spins at the end of the workout).

Also, it is loud like others have mentioned - but I think all of these kind of hoola hoops are. If you wear headphones you can easily listen to a podcast or watch youtube or something - but you can't really without headphones.

Overall, if you're looking for a weighted hoola hoop, this one is a good one!
text_fidelity_b: Smart Weighted Hula Hoops for Adults Weight Loss Non-Fall Exercise Hoola Hoop Detachable Adjustable Size Abdomen Fitness Massage Professional Intelligent Counter Workout for Women Men and Kids Blue

BIGGERFIVE Vigor 2 Kids Fitness Tracker Watch for Girls Boys Ages 5-12, IP68 Waterproof, Activity Tracker, Pedometer, Heart Rate Sleep Monitor, Calorie Step Counter Watch We have owned these smartwatches for 3 months and have had these problems since the beginning, but it's gotten steadily and rapidly worse. We now consider these unusable and are looking for better quality products.

You might be able to limp them along if you are willing to sync them with your mobile device daily/near-daily as this refreshes the data (like the time and alarms, etc). However I find the mobile app/syncing process to be tiresome - it's slow, it doesn't always save settings (the watch face is the worst offender, it changes itself seemingly at will), sometimes it takes multiple attempts to connect. I had purchased this product as it was one of the only ones which offered a "family account" and I have 2 children so I did not want to have to install the same app twice. But I still have to, essentially, "log out" of one child's settings and then sync to the other's in order to do anything like change alarms. I often wish I could make all the changes whenever it's convenient and then sync them to push those changes at a later time.

We bought this item as a test run to see if our kids would enjoy using a smartwatch enough to justify investing in decent ones. I would not recommend this item if you intend to use it long-term - save yourself the money and buy a better quality device.
text_fidelity_b: BIGGERFIVE Vigor 2 Kids Fitness Tracker Watch for Girls Boys Ages 5-12, IP68 Waterproof, Activity Tracker, Pedometer, Heart Rate Sleep Monitor, Calorie Step Counter Watch

text_fidelity_a: Hike Crew Digital Night Vision Binoculars, Capture HD Photos & Videos, See Clear in 100% Total Darkness, Long Viewing Distance, Large Viewing LCD Screen, Infrared Night Vision Goggles for Hunting It's finally getting cooler so I can sit out on my porch in the evenings.  Behind my house is a strip of wild woods - land owned by the Army Corps of Engineers as a part of the lake not too far away from my house.  Because it connects to the lake, this property has quite a bit of wildlife - coyotes, armadillos, wild pigs, deer and I've seen a large, horned owl land on a tree limb not too far from me, but I doubt I would have seen it had I not had the night vision goggles.  What is really cool is being able to snap a picture when I see something neat with them.  I really haven't tried a video, but maybe if I see an armadillo waddling past I'll take a short video - they do seem to move around more at night.  The coyotes are not shy about coming right up to my back fence which is rather creepy, but at least they don't try to jump the fence.  Anyway, having the night vision goggles has given me a new insight into what goes on just past my fence at night.  Interesting, a bit creepy, but worth knowing about for sure!

text_fidelity_a:
Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle I've had this bike a few months now. It is quiet (but not silent, there is a noise from the drive belt) but it is very smooth and responsive.

Assembly was straight-forward, but unless you want to find all the tools you need to assemble it yourself, I would recommend getting the tool package available on their website. The torque wrench was our deciding factor in just buying their kit. Keiser offers a discount on the tool package if you purchase it with the bike directly on their website.

Things to know: the app is TERRIBLE. Other reviewers have already listed all the bugs in depth, but the app is unreliable for recording workouts and is not user-friendly. The bike also will not work directly with other apps (like Peloton). For that you need the converter, which costs another $200 on top of this bike, unless you buy the bike directly from their website. Then it is only $50. Considering they were discounting it 75% with purchase of the bike, I consider $200 a rip-off for what your bike should have done in the first place (work with other apps). I wrote customer service about the bugs. They agreed there was a problem and the developer would be notified. I was told I would be updated when it was fixed. I never was. The problem in the app still persists as of my writing this review.

Customer service: I wrote customer service via email. As far as timeliness, they wrote back quickly. However, if I ever had more than one question in my message, one, and only one, of my questions would be answered. I had to write back multiple times for my additional questions to be answered, so one simple email took several days to be fully addressed. As stated above, some of the issues never were.

I will update the review if any issues with the bike itself come up. I love the bike, how smooth it runs, and the huge range of resistances available. It seems well-designed and like it will hold up. However, there are some big annoyances that will cost you extra $$$ to overcome.
text_fidelity_b: Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle

text_fidelity_a:
SABRE Runner Pepper Gel, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Reflective Hand Strap for Easy Carry & Quick Access, 35 Bursts, Secure & Easy to Use Safety, Optional Clip-On Alarm & LED Armband Combos Let's say that you are confronted by an attacker who demands something of value from you. You whip out your "police strength" red pepper get and hit him full in the face even though he is still eight feet away. After a second or two, he begins to laugh and keeps coming at you. What went wrong? The spray deployed exactly as you tested it, yet this guy seemed immune. It was made by a reputable company. And all the reviews you read were extremely positive. But what no one bothered to do was to test the formula on themselves.

Test this on myself? What kind of stupidity is this? Think of it this way. Would you buy a gun and depend on it to defend yourself and/or your family without testing it previously? Of course not. The problem here is that it's easy to test guns, knives, clubs and other weapons by hitting something with it and assessing the damage. No one gets hurt and yet you can become very comfortable by mastering the proper delivery and seeing the expected results. But pepper spray is another matter entirely. No one in their right mind wants to spray themselves in the face. Certainly not the first 21 reviewers of this product. They all seemed to be perfectly happy that the spray deployed as advertised. No offense to any of them but some of you might end up trusting your lives to this product.

But it's really pretty easy to test on yourself. I was a product development manager for a small defense corporation about 40 years ago. I had to vouch for any product that we developed and sold. Putting a defective product in the hands of someone who truly needed it (even back then) would result in a substantial lawsuit. One of the items we developed and eventually sold was one of the first self defense sprays available to the average consumer. We would pay volunteers to take a full shot in the face as we developed and improved the formula. When we began production there was always the problem of if the canisters were filled with the proper formula. Since I was unwilling to shoot myself in the face while randomly sampling dozens of these units, I would test out the sprayer on the back of my hand.

If you want to truly rely on this product, here is what you need to do. Find a sheltered (from the wind) outdoor area away from people and animals. Your back should be toward any (even) minor breeze. Hold your left hand out from your body, unfasten the safety trigger, and shoot a small stream onto the back of your hand. Hold your breath while doing so and then step away from any residual mist. Your hand should have a large orange spot on it and you should immediately feel a strong tingling or burning sensation on the back of your hand. There were no instructions that I could find that told you to shake the canister first -- so I didn't.

Unfortunately nothing happened! No stinging or burning. Even though I was just recovering from a bad cold, I put my nose within an inch of the formula and took a quick sniff. Nothing! I tried the whole exercise again after this time shaking the canister first. The results? A more consistent mixture on the back of my hand, but again no deterrent that I could detect. With my damaged and tender nose and still sore throat, i would have been expecting discomfort of an epic nature. So my guess is that this particular canister was faulty. On the other hand, no other reviewer has tested this on themselves to corroborate my findings. Perhaps the company will contact me to try and figure out why it doesn't work. This isn't my first rodeo, but it is my only shot at life. If this product failed me at the only time I really needed it, I wouldn't be around to ask for a refund.

NOTE: There was a direct sale company (We Care America) back in the late 1970's that also sold a personal defense spray. 60 Minutes (or some other news program) proved on a televised segment that the spray didn't work as advertised, taking what was once a viable company into bankruptcy. Thousands of those canisters were sold to people who believed that they were going to be adequately protected by WCA's product. That's when I knew that I had to test these things for myself.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Runner Pepper Gel, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Reflective Hand Strap for Easy Carry & Quick Access, 35 Bursts, Secure & Easy to Use Safety, Optional Clip-On Alarm & LED Armband Combos

text_fidelity_a:
Napier Backroadz SUV Tent | Universal Fits All CUV’s, SUV’s, and Minivans​ | Sleeps 5 Adults | Grey & Green | 10'x10' (19100) I got this (obviously) because I wanted to do some car camping (also, obviously). All-in-all it's a very good design and I think it will work out well for me. But it does have some issues - including a misleading description - so I'll tell you about those too.

First, by myself, it was fairly easy to set up. It's a learning experience, so make sure you set it up in your yard before you're in some dispersed campsite in BF Outer Badlands. Running the poles was straightforward, but I found that Blue Tape is your friend when attaching the main poles to the corner fittings. A second person might make the tape unnecessary, but it would still make it easier. Getting the main structure set - for the first time - took about 20 minutes, the whole set up took about an hour but I was being slow and deliberate. The inside is great and the HUGE windows provide ample ventilation. If anything the tent is too tall (which makes it tough to put the rainfly on solo) but there's plenty of room to stand everywhere in the tent. The connection with the car is good but, as others have noted, you will get some gaps (especially if you have a roof rack) that will allow bugs to get in.

Now, the big downside. The rainfly and construction is described as offering the "ultimate weather protection". Not even close. While the fly's seams are sealed, the fabric itself relies on the weave to let more water run off than soak through. The night after my initial setup there was a light dew and the rainfly was as wet on the inside as it was on the outside. The only part of the tent that seems truly waterproof is the floor. I'm planning on waterproofing the fly, the whole front door panel of the tent, any part of the tent exposed under the fly, and seal all the seams. Pay particular attention to the ground seam as it's completely exposed.

Quality control was spotty. There were some poorly stitched seams (picture) that shouldn't have made it past QC. Also, the slide locks for the fly guy ropes were incorrectly tied so I had to take them apart and retie them (picture) to keep them from slipping. Not a big deal but indicative that somebody is not paying attention. (Note: There are a couple of different ways to tie a slide lock, one of which only uses the end holes, so I don't know why they made a 3-hole lock.) The guy ropes themselves are invisible in the dark. They're flecked with white but are not reflective so another corner cut (and thing to fix...)

Bottom line is a good design with some issues that need to be fixed to make it a usable tent.

Update - I've upped it a star. I just came back from my first camping trip using the tent. It went very well. The tent is very easy to setup solo. The screen material was 100% (well, 99.99%) effective at keeping the bugs out (and it was *very* buggy) and the height of the tent makes for very comfortable living. My original comments stand as to construction, etc, but I had a problem with a weak piece of fabric which I reported to Napier. Their customer service department was amazing. They addressed the issue quickly and totally fixed things. That earned them the extra star.
text_fidelity_b: Napier Backroadz SUV Tent | Universal Fits All CUV’s, SUV’s, and Minivans​ | Sleeps 5 Adults | Grey & Green | 10'x10' (19100)

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Packs Pandion Daypack The Osprey Pandion Daypack (OPD) is the best backpack I've ever had. No detail has been overlooked. It has everything. I'm still discovering features I didn't notice over the first few days.

I use my backpack for four things - schlepping my documents and portable office supplies for work back and forth to the office, for carrying my portable electronic supplies, for clothes/toiletries etc. for short airplane trips, and for long day hikes. I did all of this and more last weekend when I traveled to New Hampshire for three days which included a four mile hike, and two days when I needed to check in at work using my laptop.

There are three main compartments, each of which has its own partitions, sleeves, a lanyard, and in one of them, a waterproof lining. The pack itself has a stiff outer frame that comes in hand for a long hike, makes it easier to stand the pack up on its own, and allows for pack to be flattened out for light cargo, or fully expanded for air travel or a large payload. There are multiple exterior sleeves for water bottles, papers, and other items that are convenient to have quick at hand. Each zipper features a plastic loop which makes them easier to grab and pull.

The pack has multiple pull tight straps in a variety of places, including waist and chest straps that makes it easier to carry heavier weight, or using the straps on the outside, compress it down for lighter trips back and forth to the office. Its got a stout handle at the top. Taught mesh fabric has been stretched between the frame in the back, which provides good comfort for toting heavier weight, and allowing air to get in behind your back as you are moving along.

It's good looking, light, and it comes with a lifetime guarantee. Please peruse the multiple photos I took of the pack a few days ago (as usual, having difficulty with Amazon photo upload functionality. I'll add photos after balance of review posts.) This is a very impressive daypack from all standpoints including function, appearance, features, and weight.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Packs Pandion Daypack

text_fidelity_a:
Ironman IFT 1000 Infrared Therapy Inversion Table This review is a commentary on my personal experience with Ironman IFT 1000; it is not a recommendation for treatment for any kind of physical ailment or injury. Please see your doctor.

Pertinent info: I'm a 5' 1", 150 lb. 65 year old woman with no other back/neck problems of which I'm aware.

I can't begin to tell you the pain I was in from a pinched nerve in my neck. For a week, I couldn't stand up for more than five minutes without my neck starting to burn and feel like someone was stabbing me. Bad enough that sometimes I really, really wanted to scream. I had to lie down on a small neck bolster with a heating pad on high to stop the pain, which took up to half a hour. Then I was stuck on my back until I was willing to endure the pain again. This was the seventh or eighth episode of this neck pain in the past couple of years, each episode worst than the last as to length and degree of pain. I missed seven days of work this time.

The success of the bolster/heat treatment is what led me to a self-diagnosis of a pinched nerve. You should see your doctor for diagnosis.

I first tried aTENS unit, which was a miserable failure for my particular condition. (I'm returning it to Amazon.) I ordered this inversion table and had friends assemble it for me since I absolutely couldn't do it. (Not nearly as simple as it looks like it should be.) I spent several hours up and down from bed making small adjustments to the unit until I had it right for me. (Tip, although I'm 5'1", the correct height setting for me on the boom arm turned out to be 5'7". I have the strap configured to allow the table to tilt no more than 35 to 40 degrees off the horizontal plane. This is FAR from completely inverted, which would be 90 degrees. However, when on the table, it feels like I'm close to upside-down.)

Once I had it adjusted to my satisfaction, I suspended myself for ten minutes, then waited to see how long it would take the pain to return while standing. 45 minutes! For someone who hadn't been able to eat anything in an upright position for a week, this was a miracle, and such a relief. Went back to bed for a couple of hours, then got back on the table again for 15 minutes. (I recommend sticking with a maximum of ten minutes as it states in the instructions.) I repeated this a couple of times in the next hour or so, sticking to ten minutes. Then I waited for the pain again. I went to bed for the night around three hours later with no pain. I woke up, got out of bed to see how long it would take the pain to hit again. When eight hours had passed and I was still pain free, I went ahead and used the table a couple of times during the remainder of the day as recommended in the instructions. That was yesterday and I'm still pain free and fixing to use the table for the first time today.

I plan on following the ten minutes, twice a day routine forever. I've read that inversion can reverse some of the damage gravity does to the internal organs over the years, compressing them and forcing them down out of their original positions. I'm hoping this will also help keep my heart, lungs, kidneys, liver, etc., from deteriorating.

I didn't buy this model for the heat function, but turns out it works just fine, at least on the first try. I'll probably not use it often, maybe in the winter to pamper myself sometimes. I'm pretty hot natured and additional heat isn't always comfortable for me. If the heat breaks, the table stays!

I'm impressed with the solid construction, the comfort of the ankle holders and the simplicity of the design. I would prefer more padding on the table, but that would probably interfere with the heat function. Attaching a piece of memory foam to the table somehow would probably work great if you don't care about the heat.

I must say that lifting my body forward to step down off the table is a little straining on my back, and someone with existing back issues might want someone else present to act as a "spotter " to aid in that, as well as to help with setting and releasing the ankle holders. You have to bend over at the waist to do that. To lean forward, I find it helps to bend my knees a little, which helps my hips act as a fulcrum. That makes it easier to lean forward to unlock the ankle holders and step off the table.

Please be aware that you may be slightly light headed when you return the table to it's upright position. Allow a few seconds for your head and inner ears to right themselves before you bend over to release the ankle holders. One final tip: If you have the slightest upset stomach, DON'T USE THE TABLE. Your stomach is likely to empty itself without warning - mine did. Probably best not to use the table on a full stomach, either. Gravity is a powerful force to move stomach contents the wrong direction, and the slight dizziness when returning to the upright position will exacerbate the problem.

I hope this review helps you make your purchasing decision.
text_fidelity_b: Ironman IFT 1000 Infrared Therapy Inversion Table

I had registered two of their motorcycle disc locks at that time and as soon as they changed the design they sent me two new replacement locks. Since then I have become older and moved from motorcycles to bicycles.

I previously submitted a review of the very excellent Saris Bike Porter 2-Bike Trunk Rack, which has design features that enable bikes to be securely locked to the rack and also allow the rack to be locked to the frame of my car, under the rear bumper. Kryptonite's 2.25' New York Noose is just the right length to lock the top tubes of two bikes to the beefy upper section of the Saris rack with their Evolution Series 4 Disc Lock, and their KryptoFlex 3/8" x 7' Double Loop Security Cable is perfect to go through the front wheels of both bikes and lock the bottom frame of the rack to the frame of my car with one of the replacement locks they sent me many years ago, which is similar to their current KryptoLok Series 2 Disc Lock. Both of these Kryptonite locks, and the chain and cable, work perfectly and I have never encountered any problems with them.

We don't need this level of security for most of our bicycle outings, but when we head out for a vacation with our bikes that includes stays at multiple motels we always use our Kryptonite locks and chains.

One final note - Although I am sure no one else at Amazon would make this foolish mistake, when we left our B&B to head home from our last vacation I locked up the bikes and then left my cord with the keys to both locks draped over one of the handle bars while I checked the pressure on our car tires for the trip home. Of course I forgot about the keys and did not notice they were missing until we got home and tried to take our bikes off the rack. Luckily I was able to go into our house and get the spare keys that came with the locks. When I ordered replacements from Kryptonite they sent me new keys for both locks at no charge. Kryptonite provides excellent locks and they also provide excellent customer service!

text_fidelity_a:
Currie Technologies Power Kit I was gifted this from a good friend of mine. Wow! It took 4 hours to install it on my Cannondale Mt Bike. I have tested it on very steep paved roads around my house and it works very well. The battery is very strong for about the 1st 2-3 miles on the hilly area. After that it will start to get a little weaker but still last me about 8 miles with hills. I weigh 216 pounds and I was running it on 2.1 knobby tires on a bike specifically designed for mountain biking - i.e. not road riding. I took it on single track to see how well it would do with some hills, does great! After having it for a couple of months, I got a flat - slow leak. I purchased a thorn resistant tire, Slime tube and Mr Tuffy liners. As other people have said, you do not want to get a flat. But I also carry all of the tools necessary to fix it out on the road just in case. I am no dummy, I have ridden thousands of road and single track miles through the years and flats are a way of life.

I can not over emphasize the ABSOLUTE JOY in riding this thing!! I had lost interest in biking because you always had to get all dolled up just to go for a ride. Not anymore. I wear jeans, Carhartt jacket if its cold and tennis shoes. Ha! I love it. Snap the battery in and I am good to go! What a great way to run to the grocery or hardware store or...

I purchased the second battery. Well worth the $100+. I can now go for a ride and when the first battery dies, click over to the second one and work my way home. I have been riding it on rough ATV trails here in Arizona and beating the heck out of the system. My rim has stayed true and the rack and batteries stay snug.

As a rap up... JOY in riding! Now I am always riding down hill. That use to be one of the things I loved about biking in Colorado where I lived. You ride up so you can ride down. Now the flat stretches are like down hills!! Woohoo! LOVE IT! I feel like a kid again... and it gets me out of the house.

Happy trails...
text_fidelity_b: Currie Technologies Power Kit

text_fidelity_a:
FINIS Swimp3 1GB Waterproof MP3 Player I bought this primarily to listen to Podcasts and some music while swimming laps. When it arrived, I was pleased with the hardware quality and ease of use. I loaded up some music and Podcasts and headed for the pool. It was relatively easy to clip the units to my goggles. The controls could be better, but are not terrible. I put it on, started playing a Podcast, put in my earplugs and started swimming. I had been concerned that my goggles might leak or come off during turns with these units clipped on, but it was not a problem at all.
The problem, though, was the sound. If sitting perfectly still underwater, it sounds decent. Pretty much on par with my 30-year-old one-speaker clock radio. However, even with earplugs, the noise of swimming and rushing water overpowers it. If I play familiar songs I can tell what I am listening to and somewhat enjoy them. However, forget about the spoken word. I had to turn the volume up really loud to be able to make out most of what was said on the Podcast due to distortion and background noise. And then it was just too loud to be enjoyable. In fact, I am sure that others in the pool could hear some sound from it. I tried to adjust it in every possible way, and followed the instructions precisely.
This seems like a good idea, but I am disappointed, especially for the cost.

Pros: Solid design, no earphones or earbuds, can still wear earplugs, easy to wear, stays on goggles and doesn't pull them off, easy to load songs.
Cons: Price, 1 GB of storage is a total insult, limited features and controls for an MP3 player, poor sound quality overshadows all else.
text_fidelity_b: FINIS Swimp3 1GB Waterproof MP3 Player

text_fidelity_a:
WataChamp Bobbin Winder (Gray) Let's start with the product quality. It appears to be very good. Well made, heavy materials, the resistance knob works well as does the line gasket. I'd say it's a good value for the price.

Next, let's talk about how it preforms. Okay, I didn't like it. Not because of the product, but due to my lack of skill. I'm attempting to make PR knots and had a real issue getting the tension right. Curls in the line because I had the tension too tight. Then knots that didn't hold because I had it too loose. I also got things tangled trying to spin it around the line and to be honest made a big mess of things. After several attempts I decided to give up.

If you want to experiment with various fishing knots this may be a good, inexpensive, way to try your hand at the techniques. However, plan on spending a lot of time and line perfecting things. It's a skill that takes plenty of time to master.

I'm not a saltwater fisherman. The heaviest line I use is #30 braid. Usually to #8-#12 leader material. I don't need a knot that holds hundreds of pounds. I'm sure if you do this is a good investment of time and money. I'll just stick with my improved Albright knot.

One last comment. I do use a wrap knot for 7 stand wire leaders on occasion. Forceps work well for that in the past, but I'm guessing this will make some really tight and clean wraps. Haven't tried it yet, but that could be the ticket.
text_fidelity_b: WataChamp Bobbin Winder (Gray)

text_fidelity_a: Antique Brass Nautical Ship Sextant Navigation Tool Pirate Marine Instrument Astrolabe Telescope with Wooden Box Two Slighting Telescope J Scott Sexton I lived on a houseboat 24/7 for 3 years - it was an experience very few people have tried and I have to admit it has its ups and downs, but I wouldn't trade the memories for anything! When I visit my grandchildren, I do like to talk to them about pursuing things or ways of life that may be different than what others tell them to (or feel they should) - I tell them about living on a boat and how many people have done the same in the past and still do and those who cruise the world and keep a sextant similar to this one just in case their electronics fail and they need to go back to how it was done in "ancient" times.  This sextant and its box have been reproduced in a faithful, authentic manner - its gorgeous and I love it!

So I drilled a hole through the door casing and was solid all the way through. Hung it up and was ready to relax. This is an overall great hammock given the price point and I cannot wait until spring to go camping with it!

text_fidelity_a: WELLFAST Survival Straw, 4 Pack Personal Water Filter with Extension Hose, 2-Stage Upgraded Portable Purification Straws for Hiking, Travel, Emergency, Camping Emergencies happen all the time - burst water pipes from freezing or just being old and then what comes out of your faucets is suspect.  I do have a filtration system to put water through should that kind of thing happening, but if you are forced to leave your home?  This set of straws are in my go-bag should I have to leave the house due to bad weather or other, similar emergency situation.  I understand these are not a magic panacea for filthy water - you want water as clean as possible and if I had to, I might even try to put together a natural filter using sand from around where I live.  At the least, the water will be clearer and I can then use one of these straws for a better, cleaner sip of water.  The real reason to have these is for the emergency you don't plan for.  They are small and easy to use, so perfect for packing in an emergency bag where my filtration system at home is not - it does a great job of filtering water, but a bit too large to stuff in a bag.  Definitely worth having on hand!

text_fidelity_a:
Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack-Red-L Used this on a 2-week service trip to East Africa. It's nice how light it is, but that also carries with it a few cons: (1) there is no "skeletal" structure to this bag...so if you load it up, gravity takes over and it sits weird against your back. I found it helpful to use a piece of thick cardboard that I would slide in first. That gave it "structure" so that it laid evenly against my back. The second con was (2) the weight-limit on the bag. Though the seems themselves never ripped, they were stretched to the max and would have easily popped had I not caught the issue early on.

Despite these two cons, for the price, and the flexibility of the bag, it's a cheap, worthy-investment. Worked as a great "personal item" for the airplane. It has a handy key ring built in, so you don't have to dig around to find your keys at the bottom of the bag. I would have liked to see a few smaller compartments within the zipped pouches, i.e. a place for a pen or two, and a few smaller items. I found myself always digging around to find my pens which made their way to the bottom, as well as my contact lens case.
text_fidelity_b: Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack-Red-L

M-Wave Plastic Bicycle Bottle Cage Black, Universal Fit The cage is great but the mount is difficult. I tried several methods of attaching to handlebars, due to slippage - no matter how tightly the grip was set. The best was some black Gorilla Tape wrapped a couple of times around the bar, then tightening down the mount as much as possible. Even then it is likely only good for a road bike, not mountain biking - for two reasons:
1. The mount, as described above, has a tendency to slip under the weight of a water bottle and some jostling
2. The cage is not adjustable and therefore probably going to work best only with the "right-sized" bottle. A smaller bottle will bounce right out. Something a small bungee will fix..

NOTE: once closed you may want to use a large screwdriver to open the mount back up.
If you are looking for a product that will not move, at all, after mounting to a bar, check out the 'Topeak CageMount' (also available through Amazon). That one works very well, even for mountain biking.

text_fidelity_a:
PBLX Dynaflex Pro Sports Gyro Wrist Exerciser, o/s n/a (10000) A few thoughts...
*Some people don't understand how to use this. After you get it going, you have to keep rocking the ball back and forth, like turning the door knob, and the point is to keep the ball steady so it's barely wobbling around in your hand.
*For best results (i think), imagine the open face pointing outwards and keep that as perpendicular to your arm as possible. DON'T do the opposite and have it facing away from you. you will not generate any speed and it will stop.
*If you loop the string more than once, you risk getting the string stuck inside the ball and you either need to open it up (screws are under the grip apparently) or cut off an end of the string. The string only needs one reinforced end anyways.
*Difficult to start by the handstrike method. String method is pretty fail-proof.
*The rubber grip on my ball says "Anytime. Anywhere." That is a load of crap. This thing is noticeably audible, like an air fan set on the medium setting. If you're looking for something discrete, move along.
*There's nothing particularly fun about this... it's just another exercise. Perhaps interesting in the beginning but not for long.
*Overall I like the product. I can certainly feel my weak grip strengthen, though I have no idea if this will really help fix the tremor I got repetitive stress. Personally, I use this in one hand while reading a book held in the other hand.
text_fidelity_b: PBLX Dynaflex Pro Sports Gyro Wrist Exerciser, o/s n/a (10000)

New Balance Lightweight Touchscreen Warm Running Gloves, Anti Slip Men's and Women's Cool Weather Gloves I use these gloves for ice skating daily. They keep my hands warm, but not too warm, and they are very comfortable. I like the rubber grips on the palms so that when I put my hands on the boards, they don't slide all over the place. The thumb and forefinger tips work well enough for my phone. Not to type, but to push play on music or skip a song..that's about the extent that you'll want to use the tips for. I got my first hole in the gloves after about 2 months of daily wear. I'm pretty tough on the gloves and they're put on and taken off multiple times a day, and frequently touch the ice or sharp skate blades...so one minor hole on a seam after that period of time seems reasonable to me. text_fidelity_a:
Synergee Farmer Walk Straps. Farmer Carry Style Straps for Loaded Carries. Sold in Pairs, 400lbs Capacity. Full Body, Functional Exercise Equipment My wife and I are not professional weight lifters and do our own stuff at home. We like to have a variety of ways to workout and we've talked about a farmer's carry before. I had the chance to grab these Synergee Farmer Walk Straps and we decided to give it a shot. For us - total amateurs - this seems like a good set up. We did a little research and know there are those who swear by things that are more bar-like, but for us at this point, these have what we need and are good for us.

The Synergee Farmer Walk Straps have a rubber handle with a decent grip to it. I've carried them with and without my workout gloves and it was fine. The materials seem to be solid and strong, well constructed, and that they'll give us longevity. I can't remember the weight limits, but we're well within I'm sure. The biggest thing for us will be getting the straps attached and lockdown well enough. You run the strap through the hole(s) on the weight you are using - we are starting with 1 X 25lbs each. Then lock it off in the buckle and wrap the rest around itself and out of the way. It's not as easy as it seemed it would be - we need practice - but it was by no means dangerous and did keep the strap out of the way and the weight secure. We'll get better. Then carrying the weight was fine - easy. We are slightly different heights, but we both felt comfortable with our first try length on the strap. That said, the one thing that IS a CON: deciding HOW LONG the strap and weight placement should be without testing and retesting. We ended up guessing and it seemed fine, nothing was hurt and hit when carrying, but it was not the easiest nor most efficient way of going about it. But it's no big deal at this point. If we get to a larger load point that exceeds that we think the straps can do - say more than 2 X 25 lbs weights that would then be swinging next to our leg, we'll maybe go for something else. We're open to seeing how this plays out. ** The last photo is me holding up the strap and handle to show the length of the strap, but not sure it shows it well enough.

So, for a beginner, we feel like this Synergee Farmer Walk Straps gets us going and on a good path, but for longer term, yes, we expect we'll outgrown these and go for something more "professional." Should one start off that way? No idea - we are unsure about the idea of the metal bar style and weight and felt this was more comfortable for getting started.
text_fidelity_b: Synergee Farmer Walk Straps. Farmer Carry Style Straps for Loaded Carries. Sold in Pairs, 400lbs Capacity. Full Body, Functional Exercise Equipment

This spoon fails the ice cream scoop test, although it puts up a fight before it bends. Since if fails that test it does not meet my needs. I did not get this for camping, which is the main use for this product. When I go camping I use plastic dinnerware which has worked fine for me.

Why does this “cutlery” set lack a knife? That is a significant omission for a "cutlery" set. $30 is too much to pay for a thin fork and spoon. These are lighter weight than flatware you would use at home, but they are about the same weight as all the other utensils designed for travel or camping. Titanium costs more because it is a rare metal, not because it is superior. If you are traveling by plane and security decides to confiscate your fork, you will be out $15.

For a $30 set that advertises that it is strong, I would expect to get a spoon that is capable of scooping premium ice cream without bending. I just reviewed a stainless-steel spoon that was of higher quality, was much stronger, and cost $3. I mainly use these for typical vacation and work travel, not multi-day hiking and camping, so weight does not matter much. If you are camping then this set is fine, but so is plastic.

text_fidelity_a:
BT Paintball Apex Barrel for Tippmann A5 Not a miracle worker by any means. The idea/concept of being able to shoot your opponents hiding behind trees and in bunkers is great in theory, but hard to execute in real life. That being said, the APEX does what it is supposed to do. Its ramping system creates spin on your ball allowing your shots to curve and bend around objects. The higher the ramp, the less the accuracy. It does increase your distance, significantly, which in my opinion makes the APEX worth it for that alone. The negative is the time it takes to take it off your barrel. With 4 little screws to remove, it's nothing you can do on the field of battle. I made the mistake of using cheap paint and paid the price. Once the paint made it into the APEX after a break, I had to remove myself from the game, get out my screw driver, take off the APEX tip, and douse it with water to clean it out.

At the end of the day, for $25, I'm pleased. Again, not a miracle worker, but allows you some creative shots that will make your opponents "think twice" before camping out behind a tree.
text_fidelity_b: BT Paintball Apex Barrel for Tippmann A5

text_fidelity_a: SPRI Women's Fitness Gloves I have been lifting weight for over 30 years and have used many different types, styles, and brands of gloves. It is a great sport for the body, but very hard on the hands. Gripping and lifting iron weights can cause major calluses across the palm of your hands. They hurt and look unsightly at the same time. Weight lifting gloves can minimize or eliminate the possibility of getting painful calluses. I had never heard of SPRI FITNESS GLOVES, but was very excited to give them a try. At first glance the look and styling is very sharp with the black glove with the simple red accent color. I usually wear leather work-out gloves and these are made from a foam/rubber material.  I am not crazy about the smell. They have a wide Velcro strap across the top of the hand that makes it easy to get them on and off, but I find it unusual to have that strap on top of the hand instead of on top of the wrist. I’m not sure if it was uncomfortable or if I am so used to having gloves that secured around my wrist.  I also like the support that you get from having gloves that close over the wrist, which these do not. They appear to be cheaply made in that the finger-tips look like they were cut off with a pair of scissors. The quality, material, and the fit are not to my satisfaction, not to mention the smell. They might break-in with repeated use, but I want a glove that is comfortable, functional, and fits well the first time I put them on.  On top of everything else. . . You have to remember what each of the colors is, but I haven't had any problems with that- green to indicate when you're checking on your steps, red to tell you your battery is getting low, and blue or purple when you're getting a phone call or text (I'm not totally sure about these as I don't use them for that). You can connect to you phone to notify you when you get a phone call or text message; you get get hourly reminders to move; you can track your sleep schedule; and what I love the most about is that you can seamlessly change activity type (running, elliptical, swimming, outdoor biking) without manipulating the information on your app.

Easy and comfortable. I have definitely found that it has helped me increase my daily steps!

text_fidelity_a:
Moultrie Error Fetching Data [[ASIN:B000VEBGBC Moultrie® Directional Feeder Kit]]

update: 2013-01-05, the unit is working well almost a year later. It spins 4 times nightly (2 or 3 seconds each time). The battery lasted until 2 weeks ago. It was still at 50%, but couldn't handle the size of the feed I put into the feeder, so it was getting clogged.
My application doesn't require food to be flung far. I have a plastic shield in front of the unit to keep the feed under the feeder. Without the shield, it tosses the feed approx 10'.

At purchase time:
Setup was pretty easy. A 5-gallon container, drill a couple of holes, add a pulley and some thin cable and you're in business.

I've had this feeder for approx 5 months. I first tried small dog food, but it clogged. Now I use small cat food and if I tilt the feeder towards the release area, it doesn't clog at all. Make sure the food is dry and you keep the lid on.

The timer works extremely well. I change it fairly often because I want to feed just after dusk and then a few more times during the night. Some feedings are 3 seconds, some are 4 seconds. 2 seconds seems to not be long enough and clogs the feeder. Atleast with the food I'm using. I have a camera on the feeding area, so I can say for sure the timer works very well.

If you have failures, you need to look at the spinner area and verify you have a clog or that the food isn't feeding down to the spinner, don't blame the timer, it's the food. Either too big or clumping.
text_fidelity_b: Moultrie Error Fetching Data

text_fidelity_a: Oakley DRT 5 Bike-Helmets As a disclaimer, I purchased this helmet as it did seem to check all of the boxes and then made the decision to buy it after finding it at a significant markdown combined with some credits from Amazon.  It was hard to pass up.  Overall I find it to be a good quality helmet.  As others have mentioned in reviews, the feel on the head is somewhat like the way a "hardhat" sits on the head- a little high center, which must have been the design.  Ventilation seems very good.  I went with size L as I am on borderline, between M and L.  But in past MTB helmet purchases,  the M felt too small.  This helmet I think I could have gone with an M and been okay.  In this case, I do wear a "bandana" or "do-rag" under the helmet.  Other reviewers commented about its weight, that it is heavier than most MTB helmets but after wearing it for rides lasting several hours, the weight of the helmet was never an issue or even a thought.  I suffered no headaches from the fit and tension of the helmet as reported by other reviewers.  Pos that stand out; 1.  it feels substantial as far as protection & MIPs, 2.  Simple design as far as headband tension system that worked well for me with the goal to be sunglass friendly.  3. comfortable.  4. Its basic design seems well made and simple (with KISS being the standard).  And so being a good basic design, it feels like it will do for which it was designed, very well.
text_fidelity_b: Oakley DRT 5 Bike-Helmets

text_fidelity_a:
Optimus Polaris Optifuel Stove, with 0.4L Fuel Bottle, multifuel Burner for Both Liquid & LPG Canister Fuel Types, for Camping, Backpacking and Emergency Preparedness PROS:
I have tested this extensively with Kerosene, isobutane canisters, propane (using the LPG Adapter/camping Propane Small Tank Input Adapter from Peakway on Amazon), and Coleman fuel. It worked great with all fuels and it boiled water quickly. In my opinion, the isobutane canister and propane tank fuel provided the most even and quiet flame--it was perfect. The Coleman fuel was right there with the isobutane and propane. As expected, the Kerosene was the most difficult to light and it provided somewhat of an uneven flame, but it was still fine, and it did not produce too much soot.

CONS:
This is not an ultra light backpacker stove by any stretch.

CONCLUSION:
I did a lot of research on this, and I am very glad I purchased it. It is made well, and I doubt it will ever break. I don't think I will ever purchase another camp stove. If you are looking for something that will use the most fuels possible, with very little maintenance, this is it.
text_fidelity_b: Optimus Polaris Optifuel Stove, with 0.4L Fuel Bottle, multifuel Burner for Both Liquid & LPG Canister Fuel Types, for Camping, Backpacking and Emergency Preparedness

Amazon Basics Portable Folding Camping Chair with Carrying Bag This camping chair is very similar to ones that I already own and enjoy. This chair is sturdy and well-made. The seat edge hits my legs further back from behind my knees than usual. Since I am 5' 4", I find this more comfortable than some bigger chairs. The seat is about 16.5" from the back seam to the front edge. The entire chair is 35" tall from floor to the back top. There is a cup holder on the right armrest. On the right side of the seat, there's a hanging magazine holder that is 10.5" across with a front, mesh flap that is 7" deep. There is an insulated cooler in the left chair arm that both zips and velcros shut, and it's 7" deep, 2.5" across, 7" high. The chair can fold up and be stored in a carry bag.

Update 5/15/18: This chair is narrower than our usual camp chairs, which means the supports/legs come through the seat right against my thighs. This will be true for most people. When my legs are tired from a long walk, sitting in this chair for more than a few minutes just makes my legs stiffer (rather than being restful) since my sore muscles partly rest against the supports. Anyway, I initially gave the chair 5 stars, but now I give it 4 stars.
